assessments.reasoning: On printed page 388, Liskov and Scheifler explicitly connect their choice of CLU to the sequential design decisions they wanted to reuse. They also identify language support for implementing both guardians and actions. The opening of section 3.1 supplies the distributed-program connection by identifying guardians as the units of program composition. The author names and journal footer identify the historical account. I reopened the retained original PDF and verified its digest, all six encoded ranges, and the decoded page against the enrolled hashes. The raw ranges anchor the page and its streams, including image data. The semantic reading comes from the page text.

challenge.method: Check whether CLU was merely an example, and whether describing guardians and actions together implies that both are units of distributed-program composition.
challenge.results: The authors report an actual choice of CLU. They identify constructs for both mechanisms, while assigning the composition role specifically to guardians. This supports the two-part design attribution within its stated limits. It establishes neither language identity nor complete semantic inheritance.

limitations: It does not claim that Argus is a CLU dialect, shares all CLU semantics, or is an alias.
